en: A brick's mass remains exactly the same on the Moon, even though its weight decreases due to lower gravity.
Water molecules can evaporate into a gas at room temperature without reaching the boiling point.
Melting an ice cube into liquid water changes its state but keeps its total mass exactly the same.
An inflated basketball has more mass than a deflated one because the trapped air inside contains matter.
Dissolving sugar in water forms a solution where the sugar's mass is still present, just spread among water molecules.
Iron rusting is a chemical change because it creates a new substance called iron oxide with different properties.
Helium gas inside a balloon expands to fill its entire volume, proving that gases have mass and take up space.
Liquid water and the steam it produces during boiling both exist at the exact same temperature of 100 degrees Celsius.
You can separate a mixture of sand and salt using physical methods like dissolving in water and filtering.
Cold air from an air conditioner is still matter because it is made of gas molecules that have mass.
Burning wood does not destroy matter, but chemically changes it into ash, water vapor, and carbon dioxide gases.
Gases like oxygen can flow and take the shape of their container, just like liquid water can.
